questions.question: The newly finalised National Designated Authority (NDA) for Carbon Markets in India is chaired by whom?

options.text: Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment Secretary.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Centre has finalised a 21-member National Designated Authority (NDA) to enable India’s carbon market, a statutory requirement under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The NDA is chaired by the Environment Secretary and includes 21 members.**
 
• **It acts as the nodal body to regulate, approve, and monitor carbon market activities in India.**
 
• **Members include representatives from Ministries of External Affairs, Steel, Renewable Energy, Power, and NITI Aayog.**
 
• **It ensures that carbon trading aligns with both domestic priorities and international climate obligations.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Functions of NDA__

 __
 
• Evaluate and approve projects generating Emission Reduction Units (ERUs).
 
• Recommend eligible activities aligned with India’s sustainability goals.
 
• Authorise ERUs for India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
 
• Monitor and update carbon market activities in line with commitments.
 
 
 
• Significance__
 __
 
• Supports India’s target of reducing emission intensity by 45% by 2030 (from 2005 levels).
 
• Encourages renewable energy and low-carbon investment.
 
 
 
• Article 6 of Paris Agreement__
 
 
• Finalised at COP29 in Baku (2024).
 
• Allows countries to trade emission reduction credits internationally.
 
• Helps nations meet NDCs cost-effectively through market mechanisms.

questions.question: Unwanted junk or unsolicited messages sent through email are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Spam mail__**.

__
 
• Spam mail

 
 
• It is also referred to as junk email, is unsolicited messages sent in bulk by email (spamming).
 
• Spammers collect email addresses from chat rooms, websites, customer lists, newsgroups, and viruses that harvest users' address books.
 
• These collected email addresses are sometimes also sold to other spammers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flag mail**

 
 
• Flagged messages create to-do items either for you alone or for you and the recipients of the email message.
 
• For example, you can flag an email message that requests information that you need by a certain date.
 
 
 
• **Push mail**
 
 
• Push email is an email system that provides an always-on capability, in which new email is actively transferred (pushed) as it arrives by the mail delivery agent (MDA) (commonly called mail server) to the mail user agent (MUA), also called the email client.
 
• Email clients include smartphones and, less strictly, IMAP personal computer mail applications.
 
 
 
• **Marked mail**
 
 
• When you mark a message as spam or phishing, it's moved from your Inbox to your Spam folder.
 
• Messages from the same sender might be sent to Spam in the future.

questions.question: Sperm are temporarily kept in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epididymis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sperm **are temporarily kept in Epididymis__**.**
 
• Each sperm cell takes between** 65-75 days to form **and around 300 million are produced every day.
 
• Inside the testes, sperm is made in structures called the seminiferous tubules.
 
• **At the top and to the back of each testicle (testis) is the epididymis, which stores sperm**.
 
• Hence, option 1 is __correct__.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In mammals, sperm cells are produced in the seminiferous tubules of each testis.
 
• These sperm cells leave the testes and pass into a larger coiled tube known as the **epididymis**.
 
• The sperm cells attain maturity in the epididymis.
 
• The sperm cells are stored in this structure till they are ejaculated.
 
• During ejaculation, **the sperms pass from the epididymis into the vas deferens and are ejaculated with the semen through the penis.**
 
• ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3c12a87fe81f99ea30c0109f707d4dbbfd05899a2e677eb40f3145d76ac209e.png] **

questions.question: The term ‘Back-stick’ is used in which of the following games/sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A number of different types of foul may be punished in a game of hockey. 

 
 
• Backsticks- This is awarded against a player who strikes the ball with the rounded back of the hockey stick.
 
• Obstruction- This is awarded against a hockey player who uses their body or stick to prevent an opponent from reaching the ball.
 
• Third-party obstruction- This is awarded when a hockey player positions themselves between the ball and an opponent, allowing a team-mate an unobstructed play on the ball.
 
• Advancing- This is awarded against a player who shoves, pushes, or advances the ball in any way, using any part of their body.
 
• Hockey stick interference- This is awarded against a player who uses their stick to hit an opponent’s stick, either intentionally or unintentionally.
 
• Undercutting- This is awarded against a player who lifts the ball in a dangerous manner.
 
• Sticks- This is awarded against a player who raises their stick dangerously near another player.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hockey players can only hit the ball with the flat side of their stick.
 
• Hence Against the player who hits the ball using the flat side of the stick is NOT considered as a type of foul in the game of hockey.

questions.question: India and Brazil recently agreed to expand the scope of their existing Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) under which Latin American economic bloc?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MERCOSUR.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India and Brazil have agreed to expand the scope of their existing Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) under the MERCOSUR bloc to include more sectors and products.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **India signed a Framework Agreement with MERCOSUR in 2003 and a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) in 2004, which came into effect in 2009.**
 
• **The agreement marked India’s first formal trade pact with a Latin American bloc, promoting bilateral and inter-regional economic cooperation.**
 
• **The expansion aims to increase trade diversification and include new product categories, strengthening India–Brazil commercial ties.**
 
• **MERCOSUR, established in 1991, is one of the largest trading blocs in the world and a key partner in India’s South-South trade strategy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• MERCOSUR (Southern Common Market)__

 __
 
• Established: 1991
 
• Founding Members: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay
 
• Headquarters: Montevideo, Uruguay
 
• Pending Member: Bolivia (awaiting full ratification)
 
• Associate Members: Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Panama (first Central American nation to join as associate)
 
 
 
• India–MERCOSUR Trade Pact__
 __
 
• Framework Agreement signed in 2003
 
• Preferential Trade Agreement signed in 2004, effective since 2009
 
• Focuses on reducing tariffs on select products and expanding trade cooperation
 
 
 
• Significance__
 
 
• Encourages South–South economic collaboration
 
• Enhances India’s access to Latin American markets
 
• Supports diversification of India’s global trade partnerships

questions.question: After how many days of absence from Parliament without permission can a Member of Parliament (MP) be disqualified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60 days.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chairman or Speaker can declare the seat vacated if a member has remained absent from all its meetings for **a period of 60 days w**i**thout** permission. While calculating the 60 days, the period for which the house is **prorogued or adjourned is not counted.**
 
• **Vacation of seats**
 
 
• Article 101 deals with it.
 
• Article 101 (4)
 
 
• If for a period of** sixty days a member of either House of Parliament** is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare** his seat vacan**t Provided that in computing the said period of sixty days no account shall be taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or is adjourned for more than four consecutive days
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 101 **

 
 
• 101(1) No person shall be a member of both Houses of Parliament and provision shall be made by Parliament by law for the vacation by a person **who is chosen a member of both Houses of his seat in one House or the other.**
 
• 101(2) No person shall be a member both of Parliament and of a House of the Legislature of a State and if a person is chosen a member both of Parliament and of a House of the Legislature of a State, **then, at the expiration of such period as may be specified in rules made by the President, that person seat in Parliament shall become vacant, unless he has previously resigned his seat in the Legislature of the State.**
 
• 103(3) If a member of either House of Parliament (a) becomes subject to any of the disqualification s mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) of Article 102, or (b)** resigns his seat by writing under his hand addressed to the Chairman or the Speaker.**

questions.question: What is the total value of the incentive scheme issued by the Ministry of Mines for the promotion of critical mineral recycling?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1,500 crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Ministry of Mines__ issued guidelines for the __₹1,500 crore__ incentive scheme aimed at promoting __critical mineral recycling__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The scheme aims to develop India’s recycling capacity for recovering critical minerals from sources like e-waste__, __spent lithium-ion batteries__, and other scrap materials.**
 
• **The guidelines include the methodology for __incentive allocation__, application procedures, and institutional oversight mechanisms.**
 
• **The scheme supports both __large and small recyclers__, including start-ups, in setting up or expanding their recycling facilities.**
 
• **The application window for the scheme remains open until __April 1, 2026__, providing ample time for eligible entities to apply.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Critical Mineral Recycling**__

 __
 
• The scheme focuses on recovering critical minerals from secondary sources, reducing dependency on primary mining.
 
• Materials like e-waste__ and __spent batteries__ are rich in valuable minerals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel.
 
 
 
• __**Support for Start-Ups and Small Recyclers**__
 __
 
• The scheme is designed to be inclusive, supporting recyclers of all sizes, particularly in the nascent stages of the recycling industry.

questions.question: Which animal has recently resurfaced in India, in Mizoram's Pualreng Sanctuary, after a gap of 108 years ?
questions.solution:
__**Correct Answer: Doria's foam-nesting tree frog has recently resurfaced in Mizoram's Pualreng Sanctuary after a gap of 108 years**__

__**Rationale**__:

__
 
• The **Doria's foam-nesting tree frog** (*Chirixalus doriae*) is an amphibian species that was rediscovered in Mizoram's **Pualreng Wildlife Sanctuary** after a significant gap of 108 years.
 
• This species was initially discovered in 1914 but had not been documented in India since then, making its reappearance a major event in the field of biodiversity conservation.
 
• The rediscovery highlights the richness of biodiversity in Mizoram and the Northeast region of India, which serves as a hotspot for unique and rare species.
 
• This frog is known for its **unique foam-nesting ability**, where it creates foam nests to protect its eggs from predators and environmental conditions.
 
• The presence of this species in Mizoram also emphasizes the need to conserve forest ecosystems and protect wildlife habitats.

**Explanation of Other Options:**__

**Snow leopard**

 
• While snow leopards are rare and elusive, they are primarily found in the Himalayan region and high-altitude areas. There is no record of snow leopards in Mizoram.

**Hyena**

 
• Hyenas are found in drier regions of India, particularly in grasslands and scrub forests. They are not native to Mizoram or its rainforests.

**Yamuna Dolphins**

 
• Yamuna dolphins refer to the **Ganges river dolphins**, which are aquatic mammals found in the river systems of northern India. They do not inhabit forest ecosystems like Mizoram's sanctuary.

**Conclusion**:

 
• The rediscovery of Doria's foam-nesting tree frog in Mizoram's Pualreng Sanctuary after 108 years underscores the importance of conservation efforts in maintaining biodiversity in India's ecologically rich regions.
 
• This finding serves as a reminder of the hidden treasures within less-explored habitats and the critical role of scientific research in documenting and protecting endangered species.

questions.question: Which among the following has been considered as 'instrument of instructions'?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is the __**Directive Principles of State Policy.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Preamble**__:

 __
 
• **The preamble is the soul of the constitution as it is the part of the constitution.**
 
• Preamble acts as an interpreter of the constitution.
 
• Whenever a question of doubt arises in the interpretation of the constitution then the matter is decided in the light of the preamble.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**:
 
 
• Articles 12-35 of Part - III of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Fundamental rights are enforceable in the court of law.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**__:
 
 
• Articles 36-51 of Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• They are borrowed from the constitution of Ireland. 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable in nature.
 
• They act as directives to the government to create any law.
 
• **They act as the ‘instrument of instructions’.**
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**:
 
 
• The fundamental duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of our constitution through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• At present, there are eleven fundamental duties under article 51 A of the constitution.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties has been borrowed from the erstwhile USSR.
 
• Originally the duties were ten in number, later on through 86th Amendment Act, 2002, the eleventh Fundamental duty was added.
 
• Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-enforceable in nature.

questions.question: Which month marks the approximate arrival of the monsoon in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Early June**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Monsoon climate in India -

__
 
• India provides the world’s most-pronounced example of a monsoon climate.
 
• The wet and dry seasons of the Indian monsoon system, along with the annual temperature fluctuations, produce three general climatic periods over much of the country:
 
 
• hot wet weather from about mid-June to the end of September,
 
• cool dry weather from early October to February,
 
• hot dry weather (though normally with high atmospheric humidity) from about March to mid-June.
 
 
 
• The actual duration of those periods may vary by several weeks, not only from one part of India to another but also from year to year.
 
• Regional differences, which are often considerable, result from a number of internal factors—including elevation, type of relief, and proximity to bodies of water.
 
• Monsoon arrives in India approximately in the month of Early June.
 
• The duration of the monsoon is between 100-120 days from early June to mid-September.
 
• The monsoon arrives at the southern part of the Indian peninsula generally by the first week of June.
 
• The season is dominated by the humid southwest summer monsoon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Tropical Monsoon climate - 

 
• Monsoons are the sea and land breezes on a larger scale.
 
• It is the seasonal reversal of wind with the change in the heating of the earth's surface. 
 
• Monsoon climate is characterized by distinct wet and dry seasons. 
 
• They can be found in the Indian sub-continent, Burma, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, parts of Vietnam and south China, and northern Australia.
 
• The basic cause of monsoon climates is the difference in the rate of heating and cooling of land and sea.

questions.question: The concept of sustainable development was emphasised internationally by

options.text: United Nations Conference on Environment and Development

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'United Nations Conference on Environment and Development.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED):**

 
 
• The concept of sustainable development was brought into the global spotlight during the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also known as the Earth Summit, held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
 
• Sustainable development focuses on meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It integrates economic, environmental, and social dimensions.
 
• The Earth Summit resulted in key documents such as the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development and Agenda 21, which outlined global strategies for sustainable development.
 
• Principles of sustainable development were discussed extensively during this conference, emphasizing the balance between economic growth, environmental protection, and social equity.
 
• The summit also led to the creation of conventions like the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), further solidifying the importance of sustainability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):**

 
 
• The WTO focuses primarily on global trade and commerce rather than environmental or sustainable development concerns.
 
• While trade policies can influence sustainability indirectly, the WTO does not spearhead global initiatives or frameworks on sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):**
 
 
• Although the UNDP actively works toward sustainable development goals (SDGs), it was not the platform that formally introduced or emphasized the concept internationally.
 
• UNDP provides resources, technical assistance, and strategies for achieving sustainable development but operates within frameworks established by conferences like UNCED.
 
 
 
• **World Bank:**
 
 
• The World Bank supports sustainable development by funding projects and programs aimed at reducing poverty and enhancing development. However, it is primarily a financial institution rather than a policymaking body for sustainable development.
 
• It implements policies rather than setting global agendas like the UNCED.
 
 
 
• **Additional Context:**
 
 
• While organizations such as the UNDP and World Bank play significant roles in promoting sustainability, the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) remains the landmark event that formally emphasized sustainable development at an international level.
 
• The conference established a global framework and principles for sustainability, influencing subsequent initiatives like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and international climate agreements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The concept of sustainable development gained traction with the Brundtland Report of 1987, officially titled "Our Common Future." This report was prepared by the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), a precursor to the discussions at UNCED.
 
• UNCED built upon the Brundtland Report’s ideas and expanded them into actionable frameworks for global cooperation.
 
• The Earth Summit is widely considered a turning point in international environmental governance and sustainable development policy.
 
• Agenda 21, a comprehensive plan of action, has been instrumental in guiding nations toward sustainable practices in development, resource management, and environmental conservation.
 
• Efforts from the Earth Summit have been carried forward through subsequent conferences, such as the Johannesburg Summit (2002) and Rio+20 (2012).
